localChanges: Computer players now settle their cities before ending the turn: when a city is about to fall into disorder, citizens are made Entertainers from its poorest tiles until it is calm, without ever starving it, and a city that did riot switches to building a Temple, Marketplace, Cathedral or Colosseum and buys what it can with up to an eighth of the treasury (#156).

log: A `PreventDisorder` strategy handles `AfterTurn`, so it runs once the player's units have moved (martial law and units away from home depend on where they stand). For each city the ruleset's `CivilDisorder` rules would flag at the next turn start, as it stands or, if it will grow then, with the extra unhappy citizen growth brings, it makes Entertainers through `library-city`'s `changeWorkedTile` from the worked tiles giving the least food, then shields, then trade, until the rules find it calm. Each pass starts by putting the previous turn's Entertainers back to work.

It never makes an Entertainer that would put the city into a food deficit, nor one needed only at the next size that would stop the city growing. A city it can't calm keeps the Entertainers that calm it as it stands (or none), and is noted with the reason (`food`, `growth`, `tiles`) in the player's memory, `uncalmedCities`, for the luxury rate (civ-clone/web-renderer#154).

A city that started the turn in disorder (`civ1-city-happiness`'s pending effect) switches to the first of Temple, Marketplace, Cathedral, Colosseum it can build, unless it has more shields in hand than that costs, and spends up to an eighth of the treasury on it, as v474.05 does: the whole purchase through `PlayerTreasury#buy` when it fits, otherwise as many shields as that buys at the ruleset's price per shield.

The generic part is `lib/City/disorder.ts`, given a `DisorderPolicy`; Civ1's is `lib/Civ1/disorder.ts`. `Dependencies` gains the specialist registries, which `civ1Knowledge.assignWorkers` now passes on.
